summary: Single-component architecture covers REQ-001..003 and the lack of interfaces is justified. The one NFR/constraint (input immutability) has a credible approach. Two minor points: float rounding risk in ceil(p/100*N) and REQ-003 having no acceptance criterion.

checklist.item: Every requirement realised by a component

checklist.note: No inter-component interfaces; public function signature percentile(scores, p) is given in REQ-001.
None needed for a single pure function.
sort() vs sorted() justified by REQ-003.

checklist.item: Integration test strategy exercises every interface
checklist.note: No interfaces; reasoning stated, unit/system tests cover behaviour.

findings.description: The rank formula ceil(p/100 x N) computed with floats can mis-round (e.g. p=29, N=100: 0.29*100 = 29.000000000000004 -> rank 30 instead of 29). The architecture does not state that the rank must be computed with exact integer arithmetic (e.g. -(-p*N // 100)). Address this in the G3 design contract and add a boundary unit test.
REQ-003 has no acceptance criteria, so system-level verification of input immutability is not anchored; add a measurable criterion (list equal to a copy of itself and same order after the call).
ASM-002 leaves NaN/non-numeric elements undefined; acceptable but should be noted in the design.
